title: 分布参数还是集总参数：先比较线长与波长
statement: 一条 300 km 长的 50 Hz 架空输电线可以看成无损耗线：特性阻抗 Z_c = 400 Ω，电磁波沿线的传播速度 v_p = 3×10⁸ m/s。始端接电源 V̇_s = 100∠0° kV（有效值），终端接 R_L = 400 Ω。
坐标 x 从始端（1–1′）量起，指向终端（2–2′）；x′ = l − x 从终端量起。

questions.ask: 架空线上电磁波的波长 λ = ?
电压波从始端传到终端需要的时间 = ?
终端电压 V̇_2 的初相 = ?（V̇_s 的初相为 0°）
questions.explain: 负载等于特性阻抗时线上只有入射波：V̇(x) = V̇_1·e^{−jβx}。βl = 2π·l/λ = 2π × 0.05 rad = 18°，所以 V̇_2 滞后 V̇_1 18°，初相 −18°。

questions.ask: 取 v_p = 2×10⁸ m/s（电缆、印制板走线中常见），下面哪一种必须按分布参数电路（传输线）分析？
choices: 2 m 长的音频线，信号 20 kHz
0.3 m 长的印制板走线，信号 1 GHz
楼内 1 km 长的照明线路，50 Hz
choiceExplain: λ = 2×10⁸/2×10⁴ = 10 km，l/λ = 2×10⁻⁴，可以看成集总参数电路。
λ = 0.2 m，l/λ = 1.5，沿线各处电压的相位完全不同——这是分布参数电路。
λ = 4000 km，l/λ = 2.5×10⁻⁴，集总参数电路足够。
questions.explain: 判断标准是 l 与 λ 的比值，而不是 l 本身有多长。0.3 m 走线在 1 GHz 下 λ = 0.2 m，l = 1.5λ，沿线电压电流的相位差很大，必须用传输线方程。

hints: 判断一个电路能不能当集总参数电路处理，要看它的尺寸和工作波长 λ 的比值。
λ = v_p/f；波从一端传到另一端用的时间是 l/v_p。
R_L = Z_c 时线上只有入射波，沿线电压大小不变，相位按 βx 滞后，β = 2π/λ。
solution: **4. 终端电压的相位。** R_L = Z_c（匹配），线上只有入射波 V̇(x) = V̇_1·e^{−jβx}，V̇_2 = 100∠**−18°** kV：大小不变，相位滞后 βl。
**5. 结论。** 300 km 的 50 Hz 线路只有 0.05λ，已经能看出明显的相位差（18°），所以超高压长线要按分布参数处理；而几米长的低频线路 l/λ 极小，集总参数模型足够。判断时总是看 l/λ。
**检查：** 18° 对应的时间 = 18/360 × 20 ms = 1 ms，与传播时间一致 ✓。

en.title: Distributed or lumped? Compare the length with the wavelength first
statement: A 300 km, 50 Hz overhead transmission line may be treated as lossless: characteristic impedance Z_c = 400 Ω, propagation speed v_p = 3×10⁸ m/s. The start is fed by V̇_s = 100∠0° kV (rms) and the end is loaded with R_L = 400 Ω.
x is measured from the start (1–1′) towards the end (2–2′); x′ = l − x is measured from the end.

questions.ask: Wavelength on the overhead line, λ = ?
Time for a wave to travel from the start to the end = ?
questions.explain: t = l/v_p = 3×10⁵/(3×10⁸) = 1 ms, i.e. 1/20 of the 50 Hz period (20 ms).

questions.ask: Initial phase of the end voltage V̇_2 = ? (V̇_s has phase 0°)
questions.explain: With the load equal to the characteristic impedance only the incident wave exists: V̇(x) = V̇_1·e^{−jβx}. βl = 2π·l/λ = 2π × 0.05 rad = 18°, so V̇_2 lags V̇_1 by 18°: phase −18°.

questions.ask: With v_p = 2×10⁸ m/s (typical of cables and PCB traces), which one must be analysed as a distributed-parameter circuit (a transmission line)?
choices: A 2 m audio cable carrying 20 kHz
A 0.3 m PCB trace carrying 1 GHz
A 1 km lighting circuit in a building at 50 Hz
questions.explain: What matters is l compared with λ, not l itself. At 1 GHz λ = 0.2 m, so the 0.3 m trace is 1.5λ long: the voltage phase changes completely along it and the line equations are needed.
choiceExplain: λ = 2×10⁸/2×10⁴ = 10 km, l/λ = 2×10⁻⁴: a lumped circuit is fine.
λ = 0.2 m, l/λ = 1.5: the voltage has a different phase at every point — a distributed circuit.
λ = 4000 km, l/λ = 2.5×10⁻⁴: a lumped model is enough.

hints: Whether a circuit may be treated as lumped depends on its size compared with the operating wavelength λ.
λ = v_p/f; a wave needs l/v_p to travel from one end to the other.
With R_L = Z_c only the incident wave exists: its amplitude is constant along the line and its phase lags by βx, β = 2π/λ.
solution: **4. Phase of the end voltage.** R_L = Z_c (matched): only the incident wave V̇(x) = V̇_1·e^{−jβx}, so V̇_2 = 100∠**−18°** kV — same magnitude, phase lagging by βl.

**5. Conclusion.** A 300 km line at 50 Hz is only 0.05λ long yet already shows an 18° phase shift, so long EHV lines are distributed circuits; a few metres of low-frequency wiring have a tiny l/λ and the lumped model is enough. Always judge by l/λ.
**Check:** 18° corresponds to 18/360 × 20 ms = 1 ms, the travel time ✓.
